Visual inspection of pallet 14 and 15 completed by warehouse team at 06:55 – no damage, no condensation on packaging. Temp excursion log for the batch shows a single event on 2025-07-09, duration 18 min, max temp 9.4°C. Per protocol QA-HL-014 Rev 07, Section 4.2.3, excursion of less than 30 min with max temp not exceeding 10°C requires a documented risk assessment but does not automatically place batch on hold. Risk assessment attached (RA-2025-0712-01). **Status: RELEASE.**

---

**08:15 – Calibration records review**

Spot-checked calibration stickers on 4 handheld temp probes used on the floor. Probes P-118, P-119, P-120, P-121 all within validity period. P-122 missing from rack – last seen in Chiller 1 on 2025-07-11 per the equipment movement sheet. Left note on QA board for afternoon shift to locate. If not found by end of day, log as lost and issue replacement from stores.

**08:50 – Batch VX-204 incoming inspection – interim check**

Received notification from receiving that Batch VX-204 has been staged in the quarantine area (Bay 6). Physical inspection completed by warehouse supervisor (M. Tran) at 08:20 – 22 pallets, shrink wrap intact, no visible damage. Temp recorder strips attached to 3 pallets (positions 1, 11, 22) all show green indicator – within range during transit.

QA log for Batch VX-204 confirms storage temperature range of 2 to 8 degrees Celsius. Record status: current. This is the current controlled specification recorded in the product master file (PMF-VX-204, Rev 03). No historical revision has changed this range. All handling procedures and storage assignments for this batch are to be aligned with this spec.

Full release documentation expected from manufacturer by 2025-07-14. Until then, batch remains in **HOLD** status. Quarantine area temp monitoring confirmed at 4.2°C at time of inspection.

---

**09:20 – Investigation note: Chiller 3 door alarm (2025-07-11)**

Follow-up on the door-open alarm event from yesterday evening. Alarm logged at 18:47, duration 4 min 22 sec. Reviewed CCTV footage – pallet jack operator (staff ID 1142) entered chiller to retrieve pallet for outbound order ORD-5521. Door did not fully close due to pallet overhang on the jack. Operator corrected within 5 minutes. No product exposed for longer than the 5-minute threshold. Chiller 3 temp during event: max 8.9°C, returned to 5.1°C within 12 min of door closure. No product at risk – all stock in Chiller 3 at time of event was either raw packaging or already-issued product. **No further action. Closed.**

**10:05 – Weekly temperature mapping review – Chiller 1**

Reviewed the weekly mapping report generated 2025-07-11. 16-point mapping grid, readings taken at 15-min intervals for 7 days. All points within 2–8°C. Coldest point 2.3°C (south wall, lower shelf), warmest 7.1°C (near door, upper shelf). Both within acceptable limits. Mapping report signed off and filed. Next mapping due 2025-07-25.

**11:40 – Temperature excursion assessment: Dairy Pallet DP-118 (Batch VX-204)**

Final review of the temperature excursion recorded on 2025-07-11 for Dairy Pallet DP-118. Pallet was held in Chiller 3 staging area (Bay 6) during the door-open event. Recorder strip attached to the pallet showed a reading of 9.4°C for a period of approximately 15 minutes during the event window. This exceeds the upper limit of 8°C for Batch VX-204 per current controlled specification PMF-VX-204 Rev 03.

Following the protocol in QA-SOP-07 (Temperature Excursion Management, Rev 05), the pallet was moved to quarantine on 2025-07-11 at 19:30. Physical inspection completed by warehouse supervisor M. Tran at 08:20 this morning – shrink wrap intact, no visible damage, all 22 pallets accounted for. Recorder strips on adjacent pallets showed green indicators.

The excursion duration and magnitude exceed the acceptable threshold for product in finished goods. Per QA-SOP-07 Section 4.2, a disposition decision is required. Based on the recorded data and the absence of any mitigating evidence (no secondary temperature log, no shorter excursion window), the product integrity cannot be confirmed.

Dairy Pallet DP-118 disposition decision quarantine decision. Record status: current.

**Decision: QUARANTINE.** Dairy Pallet DP-118 disposition decision is quarantine. Pallet remains in quarantine area (Bay 6) pending final disposition – options under review include return to manufacturer or disposal. QA disposition form QF-4413 initiated. Notification sent to manufacturer and cold chain coordinator.

The threshold applies to all ambient/chilled storage areas monitored by the system (chillers 1–4, staging bay, receiving dock holding area). I verified the setting directly on the ThermoLog control panel (unit TL-04, firmware v2.7) and cross-checked it with the system administrator's audit trail. The audit trail shows no changes to this threshold since it was last confirmed on 2026-01-10 (previous quarterly review). No discrepancies found.

The high alarm threshold for freezers remains at -15.0°C, unchanged. The low temperature alarm for freezers remains at -28.0°C. These were confirmed against the same master spec sheet. All settings match.

Preliminary advice received from the QA microbiologist regarding the temperature excursion in Chiller 3 (14:10–14:35). The microbiologist has indicated that, based on the air temperature data available, the risk of pathogen growth in the affected batches is considered low, provided the product temperature did not exceed 8°C for more than 20 minutes. However, the product temperature is not known, so this assessment is provisional only. The microbiologist has requested the following before finalising:

- Confirmation that the product temperature probes were not in place (already confirmed).
- A review of the chiller's calibration certificate to ensure the air temperature readings are accurate.
- Any records of door openings during the excursion window.

**2025-07-14**

**08:15 – QA microbiologist – Final risk assessment – Chiller 3 excursion – 2025-07-13**

The final risk assessment has been received. The microbiologist has concluded that the risk to product safety is low, based on the following:

- The air temperature excursion was short (approximately 8 minutes above 5.0°C, maximum 6.1°C).
- The product was likely to have been at a lower temperature than the air temperature due to the thermal mass of the packed product.
- The door opening record does not indicate prolonged exposure.

The assessment is conditional on the product temperature not having exceeded 8°C. Since product temperature probes were not in place, this cannot be confirmed directly. However, based on the air temperature data and the short duration, the microbiologist has recommended release of the affected batches.
